tests.title: PUT with no body, {} or secret null generates a 64-hex secret, stores it and returns it once
given: an active workspace widgets owned by the caller
a real secrets store on an in-memory SQLite database
external_url is https://hub.example.com
tests.when: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/forge/webhook is called three times, with no body, with {} and with {"secret":null}
then: each answer is 200
the body has configured true, url https://hub.example.com/hooks/forge/widgets and a secret of exactly 64 lowercase hex characters
GetSecretValue("workspace","widgets","FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET") equals the returned secret after each call
two generated secrets differ
tests.pseudocode: for body in [none, '{}', '{"secret":null}']: r = put(body); assert r.status==200; assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$', r.json.secret); assert store.Get('workspace','widgets','FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET') == r.json.secret

tests.title: A supplied valid secret is stored and not echoed back
given: an active workspace widgets owned by the caller
tests.when: PUT …/forge/webhook is called with secrets of length 16, 40 and 255 made of printable ASCII from '!' to '~'
then: each answer is 200 with configured true and a url field
the body has no secret key
the stored value equals the supplied value
tests.pseudocode: for s in [rand(16), rand(40), rand(255)]: r = put({'secret': s}); assert r.status==200; assert 'secret' not in r.json; assert store.Get(...) == s

tests.title: Invalid PUT bodies answer 400 naming secret without echoing the value and store nothing
given: an active workspace widgets that already has the secret 'existing-secret-value'
tests.when: PUT is called with a JSON array body, malformed JSON, {"secret":123}, a 15-character secret, a 256-character secret, a secret containing a space and a secret containing a control character
then: every answer is 400 via the apikit error envelope
the message names secret and the violated rule
the message does not contain the supplied value
the stored secret is still 'existing-secret-value'
tests.pseudocode: for body in invalid: r = put(body); assert r.status==400; assert 'secret' in r.msg; assert supplied not in r.msg; assert store.Get(...)=='existing-secret-value'

tests.title: PUT checks credential, scope, ownership and status in order and stops at the first failure
given: workspace widgets owned by user A and active
workspace old owned by user A and archived
a secrets store wrapper that records calls
tests.when: PUT is called with no credential, with a PAT lacking forge:write, as user B on widgets, and as user A on archived old, each with an invalid body
then: the answers are 401, 403, 404 and 400 respectively
the 403 message names forge:write
the 400 message is 'workspace is not active'
the body is never validated (no 'secret' rule message) and the secrets store is never called
tests.pseudocode: assert put(noauth).status==401; r=put(pat_read_only); assert r.status==403 and 'forge:write' in r.msg; assert put(userB).status==404; r=put(archived); assert r.status==400 and r.msg=='workspace is not active'; assert store.calls==0

tests.title: PUT updates an existing secret and retries once after a concurrent create conflict
given: a workspace whose scope already has FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=old
a second workspace where CreateSecrets returns *ConflictError once because another request created the key
tests.when: PUT is called with a new valid secret on each workspace
then: both answers are 200
exactly one FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET entry exists in the scope
the stored value is the new secret
UpdateSecret is called at most twice in the conflict case
tests.pseudocode: put({'secret': new}); assert len(store.List('workspace', slug) where key=='FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET')==1; assert store.Get(...)==new

tests.title: A full secrets scope answers 400 with the store message and other store failures answer 500, with no event
given: a workspace whose scope holds 100 secrets
a store stub whose UpdateSecret fails with a generic error
a recording emitter
tests.when: PUT …/forge/webhook is called against each
then: the full scope answers 400 carrying 'maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded'
the generic failure answers 500
the recording emitter holds no hub.forge.webhook.set event
tests.pseudocode: r=put(full); assert r.status==400 and 'maximum of 100 entries' in r.msg; r=put(broken); assert r.status==500; assert emitter.events==[]

tests.title: The ingress URL trims a trailing slash and is null when external_url is unset while the secret is still stored
given: external_url configured as https://hub.example.com/ in one run and empty in another
tests.when: PUT …/forge/webhook is called for workspace widgets in each configuration
then: with the configured value url equals https://hub.example.com/hooks/forge/widgets
with an empty value url is JSON null
in both cases the secret is stored
tests.pseudocode: assert put().json.url=='https://hub.example.com/hooks/forge/widgets'; cfg.ExternalURL=''; r=put(); assert r.json.url is None; assert store.Get(...) != ''

tests.title: A successful PUT emits hub.forge.webhook.set with only the generated flag
given: a recording emitter in forge.Config.Audit
tests.when: PUT is called once with no body and once with a supplied secret
then: two hub.forge.webhook.set events are recorded with workspace widgets
metadata is exactly {generated:true} for the first and {generated:false} for the second
no metadata value contains the secret
tests.pseudocode: assert events[0].Metadata=={'generated':True}; assert events[1].Metadata=={'generated':False}

tests.title: DELETE removes the secret, answers 204 whether or not it existed and works on archived workspaces
given: an active workspace with the secret set
an archived workspace with the secret set
an active workspace without the secret
a recording emitter
tests.when: DELETE …/forge/webhook is called on each workspace
then: every answer is 204 with an empty body
the secret is gone on the first two workspaces
hub.forge.webhook.unset events carry existed true, true and false respectively
tests.pseudocode: for ws in three: assert delete(ws).status==204; assert [e.Metadata['existed'] for e in events]==[True,True,False]

tests.title: DELETE answers 401, 403, 404 on auth failures without touching the store and 500 on a store failure
given: a secrets store wrapper that records calls and can fail DeleteSecret with a generic error
tests.when: DELETE is called with no credential, with a PAT lacking forge:write, as a non-owner, and with a failing store
then: answers are 401, 403 (message names forge:write), 404
the store is not called in the first three cases
the failing store answers 500
tests.pseudocode: assert delete(noauth).status==401; ...; assert delete(broken).status==500

tests.title: After DELETE a delivery answers 404 identical to an unknown slug and old rows remain listed
given: workspace widgets with a secret and one recorded delivery row
ingress and API routes registered on one Echo instance with a real SQLite database
tests.when: DELETE …/forge/webhook is called, then a signed delivery is posted to /hooks/forge/widgets, then GET …/forge/deliveries is called
then: the delivery answers 404 with the same body as an unknown slug
no new row is written
GET deliveries still returns the earlier row
tests.pseudocode: delete(); r=post_signed(); assert r.status==404 and r.body==post('/hooks/forge/nosuch').body; assert len(get_deliveries())==1

tests.title: GET /forge carries a webhook block with configured, url and last_delivery_at and sends nothing to the forge
given: workspace A with a secret and delivery rows received_at 09:00 (ignored) and 09:12 (malformed)
workspace B with no secret and no rows
a forge transport that fails the test on any request
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/forge is called for A and B
then: A has webhook.configured true, the ingress URL and last_delivery_at equal to the 09:12 timestamp
B has configured false, url present or null per external_url and last_delivery_at null
no outbound forge request was made
tests.pseudocode: a=get('A'); assert a.webhook=={'configured':True,'url':url,'last_delivery_at':'…09:12:00Z'}; b=get('B'); assert b.webhook.configured==False and b.webhook.last_delivery_at is None

tests.title: A secrets or delivery-log failure on GET /forge answers 500 with no partial webhook block
given: one run with a secrets store that fails with a generic error
one run with the forge_deliveries table dropped
tests.when: GET …/forge is called in each run
then: both answers are 500 via the apikit envelope
the body has no webhook key
tests.pseudocode: assert get().status==500 and 'webhook' not in get().json

tests.title: The secret value never appears outside the response of the PUT that generated it
given: captured slog output, a real audit store and a real delivery log
tests.when: for any valid secret value (generated or supplied, 16 to 255 printable ASCII characters), PUT then GET /forge, GET /forge/deliveries, GitHub and GitLab deliveries (accepted and rejected), and DELETE are executed
then: the secret string occurs in no GET /forge body, deliveries body, DELETE response, ingress response, log line, hub_audit_events metadata or forge_deliveries row
for a generated secret it occurs only in the PUT response
tests.pseudocode: for s in gen_secrets(): run_all(s); for sink in [responses_except_put, logs, audit_metadata, delivery_rows]: assert s not in str(sink)

tests.title: POST /hooks/forge/:slug is served on the Echo root without bearer authentication
given: an Echo instance with the API group protected by bearer authentication and the ingress mounted on the root, no lock manager supplied
a forge transport that fails on any request
tests.when: a signed delivery without an Authorization header is posted to /hooks/forge/widgets and an unauthenticated GET is made to an API route
then: the delivery reaches the handler and answers 202
the API route answers 401
no workspace lock was taken and no forge request was made
tests.pseudocode: assert post_signed(no_auth).status==202; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/widgets/forge').status==401

tests.title: Unknown slug and missing workspace-scope secret give byte-identical 404 before the body is read, and lookup failures give 500
given: workspace nosecret without a secret but with an org-scoped and a user-scoped FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
a body reader that fails the test if read
a variant where the workspaces table is missing
tests.when: a delivery is posted to /hooks/forge/nosuch and /hooks/forge/nosecret, then to a slug during a database failure
then: both first answers are 404 with identical bytes
the body is never read
no row and no event are written
the failure case answers 500
tests.pseudocode: a=post('/hooks/forge/nosuch'); b=post('/hooks/forge/nosecret'); assert a.status==404 and a.body==b.body; assert post(dbfail).status==500

tests.title: A GitHub delivery is accepted only with sha256= plus the exact 64-hex HMAC of the body
given: workspace widgets with secret S and a valid issues labeled body
tests.when: deliveries carry the correct signature, a signature over a different body, a signature with another key, a header without the sha256= prefix, a 63-digit hex, non-hex characters, and an uppercase-hex correct digest
then: the correct signature answers 202
every wrong or malformed one answers 401 'delivery signature missing or invalid'
the signature check uses the raw bytes received
tests.pseudocode: assert post(sig='sha256='+hmac(S,body)).status==202; for bad in variants: assert post(sig=bad).status==401

tests.title: A GitLab delivery is accepted only when X-Gitlab-Token equals the secret and the token is checked before the body is read
given: workspace widgets with secret S
a body reader that records whether it was read
tests.when: a delivery with a wrong X-Gitlab-Token and a delivery with the correct token are posted
then: the wrong token answers 401 and the body was not read
the correct token answers 202
when both X-Hub-Signature-256 and X-Gitlab-Token are present the GitHub scheme is used
tests.pseudocode: r=post(token='x', body=tracking); assert r.status==401 and not body.read; assert post(token=S).status==202

tests.title: Unverified deliveries answer 401 with one message, record nothing and log only slug and scheme
given: workspace widgets with a secret
captured slog output
empty forge_deliveries and hub_audit_events
tests.when: deliveries are posted with no scheme header, a wrong GitHub signature, a malformed signature and a wrong GitLab token
then: each answer is 401 with the message 'delivery signature missing or invalid'
forge_deliveries and hub_audit_events row counts are unchanged
a warn-level log line carries slug and scheme
no log line contains a header value or the body
tests.pseudocode: for req in bad: r=post(req); assert r.status==401 and r.msg=='delivery signature missing or invalid'; assert count(deliveries)==0; assert header_value not in logs and body not in logs

tests.title: A body over 1 MiB or over max_body_size answers 413, the handler's own with body_too_large
given: workspace widgets with a secret
one Echo instance with max_body_size raised above 1 MiB and one with the 1MB default
tests.when: a correctly signed delivery of 1048577 bytes is posted (chunked and with Content-Length), and one of exactly 1048576 bytes
then: the oversize deliveries answer 413
with the raised global limit the 413 carries error_type body_too_large
no row and no event are written
the delivery of exactly 1048576 bytes passes the size check
tests.pseudocode: r=post_signed(size=1<<20+1); assert r.status==413 and r.error_type=='body_too_large'; assert count(rows)==0

tests.title: A rotated secret applies from the next delivery with no caching
given: workspace widgets with secret OLD accepted once
a real secrets store
tests.when: the secret is rotated to NEW through PUT …/forge/webhook and the secrets CLI path, then deliveries signed with OLD and NEW are posted
then: the OLD-signed delivery answers 401
the NEW-signed delivery answers 202
tests.pseudocode: put({'secret':NEW}); assert post(sign(OLD, body, id='d2')).status==401; assert post(sign(NEW, body, id='d3')).status==202

tests.title: An archived workspace with a secret verifies, records and relays like an active one
given: an archived workspace widgets with a secret and origin repo acme/widgets
a recording emitter
tests.when: a signed GitHub issues labeled delivery for acme/widgets is posted
then: the answer is 202 {"outcome":"relayed"}
one row is recorded
hub.forge.issue.labeled is emitted
tests.pseudocode: r=post_signed(); assert r.status==202 and r.json.outcome=='relayed'; assert len(emitter.events)==1

tests.title: InitSchema creates forge_deliveries with its key and index idempotently without touching rows
given: an empty SQLite database
tests.when: forge.InitSchema is called, a row is inserted, and InitSchema is called again
then: both calls return nil
table forge_deliveries has the nine listed columns, primary key (workspace_slug, delivery_id) and an index on (workspace_slug, received_at)
the row count is unchanged and inserting the same key twice conflicts
tests.pseudocode: assert InitSchema(db)==nil; insert(row); assert InitSchema(db)==nil; assert count==1; assert pragma_table_info columns == expected

tests.title: A verified delivery records one row with ids and event taken from the right headers
given: workspace widgets with a secret
an event name longer than 64 bytes in one GitHub case
tests.when: a GitHub issues labeled delivery, a GitLab delivery with both Idempotency-Key and X-Gitlab-Event-UUID, a GitLab delivery with only X-Gitlab-Event-UUID, and the long event name delivery are posted
then: each produces exactly one row
delivery_id equals X-GitHub-Delivery, Idempotency-Key, and X-Gitlab-Event-UUID respectively
forge is github or gitlab, event is the header value cut to 64 bytes, action is the payload action or empty, target is origin, relayed is a JSON array of event types
received_at is a UTC timestamp
tests.pseudocode: assert row.delivery_id=='gh-1'; assert json.loads(row.relayed)==['hub.forge.issue.labeled']; assert len(row.event.encode())<=64

tests.title: A verified delivery without id or event name, or with an invalid id, answers 400 and records nothing
given: workspace widgets with a secret
tests.when: signed deliveries are posted with no X-GitHub-Delivery, no X-GitHub-Event, a GitLab delivery with neither id header, a 256-character id and an id containing a non-ASCII character
then: each answer is 400 via apikit.WriteAPIError
forge_deliveries row count is unchanged and no event is emitted
a 255-character id is accepted
tests.pseudocode: for req in bad: assert post(req).status==400; assert count(rows)==0; assert post(id='a'*255).status==202

tests.title: A repeated delivery id answers 202 duplicate with no new row and no event
given: workspace widgets with a secret and a recording emitter
one prior accepted delivery gh-1
tests.when: the same signed delivery with id gh-1 is posted again
then: the answer is 202 {"outcome":"duplicate"}
row count stays 1
the emitter holds only the events of the first delivery
tests.pseudocode: post(); r=post(); assert r.json=={'outcome':'duplicate'}; assert count(rows)==1; assert len(emitter.events)==1

tests.title: A delivery-log insert failure answers 500 with no event and a redelivery is then processed in full
given: workspace widgets with a secret and a recording emitter
forge_deliveries dropped so the insert fails
tests.when: a signed delivery is posted, the table is recreated and the same delivery is posted again
then: the first answer is 500 via the apikit envelope and no hub.forge.* event was emitted
the second answer is 202 relayed with one row and one event
tests.pseudocode: drop(); assert post().status==500; assert emitter.events==[]; InitSchema(db); assert post().json.outcome=='relayed'

tests.title: N copies of one delivery, including concurrent ones, record one row and relay once
given: workspace widgets with a secret and a recording emitter
tests.when: for any N from 1 to 20, N copies of the same signed delivery id are posted concurrently
then: exactly one forge_deliveries row exists
the events of the delivery are emitted exactly once
exactly one answer is relayed and N-1 answers are duplicate
tests.pseudocode: for n in range(1,21): res = parallel(post, n); assert count(rows)==1; assert counter(res.outcome)=={'relayed':1,'duplicate':n-1}; assert len(emitter.events)==1

tests.title: A non-object body or a missing required field is recorded as malformed and answered 400
given: workspace widgets with a secret and a recording emitter
tests.when: signed deliveries are posted with a body of [], of 'null', of invalid JSON, and with a GitHub issues payload lacking issue.number
then: each answer is 400
one forge_deliveries row with outcome malformed is written per delivery
nothing is emitted
tests.pseudocode: for b in bad: assert post(b).status==400; assert [r.outcome for r in rows]==['malformed']*4; assert emitter.events==[]

tests.title: Unmapped event and action pairs are recorded ignored, answered 202 and emit nothing
given: workspace widgets with a secret and a recording emitter
tests.when: GitHub ping, pull_request labeled and issue_comment edited, GitLab Confidential Issue Hook, Confidential Note Hook and a Note Hook on a Commit are posted
then: each answer is 202 {"outcome":"ignored"}
each is recorded with outcome ignored and relayed []
nothing is emitted
tests.pseudocode: for d in cases: assert post(d).json=={'outcome':'ignored'}; assert emitter.events==[]

tests.title: A repository equal to origin ignoring case binds the delivery to origin
given: workspace git_url https://forge.example.com/Acme/Widgets.git
a nested GitLab namespace variant group/sub/widgets
tests.when: a GitHub delivery with repository.full_name acme/widgets and a GitLab delivery with project.path_with_namespace group/sub/Widgets are posted
then: rows have target origin
event metadata target is origin
tests.pseudocode: assert row.target=='origin'; assert event.Metadata['target']=='origin'

tests.title: On a carry_patch workspace a delivery for the upstream repository binds to upstream
given: carry_patch workspace with git_url …/acme/widgets and upstream_url …/upstream/widgets
tests.when: a signed delivery with repository.full_name upstream/widgets is posted
then: the answer is 202 relayed
the row target and event metadata target are upstream
tests.pseudocode: post(repo='upstream/widgets'); assert row.target=='upstream' and event.Metadata['target']=='upstream'

tests.title: A delivery for an unrelated repository or with an unparseable remote is a repository_mismatch
given: a workspace with origin acme/widgets
a standard workspace that has an upstream_url
a carry_patch workspace without upstream_url
a workspace whose git_url cannot be parsed
tests.when: signed deliveries for other/repo, for the upstream repo on the standard workspace, for an upstream repo on the carry_patch workspace without upstream_url, and for any repo on the unparseable workspace are posted
then: each answer is 202 {"outcome":"repository_mismatch"}
each row has outcome repository_mismatch and NULL target
no event is emitted
tests.pseudocode: for ws in cases: r=post(ws); assert r.json.outcome=='repository_mismatch'; assert row.target is None; assert emitter.events==[]

tests.title: GitHub issues actions map to the six hub.forge.issue.* events
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter

then: each yields exactly one event of type hub.forge.issue.<action>
each outcome is relayed
tests.pseudocode: for a in actions: post(issues, a); assert [e.EventType for e in emitter.events]==['hub.forge.issue.'+a for a in actions]

tests.title: GitHub issue_comment created maps to comment.created with the pull_request flag
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: an issue_comment created delivery is posted once with issue.pull_request present and once without
then: two hub.forge.comment.created events are emitted
metadata pull_request is true for the first and false for the second

tests.title: GitHub pull_request actions map to opened, reopened, synchronize and merged or closed
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: pull_request deliveries with opened, reopened, synchronize, closed with merged true and closed with merged false are posted
then: events are pull_request.opened, .reopened, .synchronize, .merged and .closed in that order
the merged pull request never yields .closed
tests.pseudocode: assert types==['…opened','…reopened','…synchronize','…merged','…closed']

tests.title: A GitHub push delivery maps to hub.forge.push
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: a signed push delivery with ref, before and after is posted
then: exactly one hub.forge.push event is emitted
the outcome is relayed
tests.pseudocode: assert [e.EventType for e in events]==['hub.forge.push']

tests.title: GitLab Issue Hook open, close and reopen map to opened, closed and reopened
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: Issue Hook deliveries with object_attributes.action open, close and reopen are posted with the correct token
then: events hub.forge.issue.opened, .closed and .reopened are emitted, one per delivery
number is the object_attributes iid
tests.pseudocode: assert types==['hub.forge.issue.opened','hub.forge.issue.closed','hub.forge.issue.reopened']

tests.title: GitLab Issue Hook update emits edited, then unlabeled, then labeled, each group sorted by name
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: an update delivery changes the title, removes labels z and b and adds labels y and a, and a second update only adds A and removes B
then: the first delivery emits edited, unlabeled(b), unlabeled(z), labeled(a), labeled(y) in that order
the second emits unlabeled(B) then labeled(A)
labeled and unlabeled events carry the label name in metadata label

tests.title: A GitLab issue update with no title, description or label change is ignored
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: an Issue Hook update with an empty changes object and one whose labels previous equals current are posted
then: each answer is 202 {"outcome":"ignored"}
nothing is emitted
tests.pseudocode: assert post(update_no_change).json.outcome=='ignored'; assert emitter.events==[]

tests.title: GitLab Note Hook on Issue or MergeRequest maps to comment.created with the right number and flag

then: two hub.forge.comment.created events are emitted
numbers are 7 and 9 and pull_request is false then true

tests.title: GitLab Merge Request Hook maps open, close, reopen, merge and update with or without oldrev
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: Merge Request Hook deliveries with open, close, reopen, merge, update with oldrev and update without oldrev are posted
then: events are pull_request.opened, .closed, .reopened, .merged and .synchronize
the update without oldrev answers 202 ignored and emits nothing

tests.title: GitLab Push Hook and Tag Push Hook map to hub.forge.push
given: a bound workspace and a recording emitter
tests.when: a Push Hook and a Tag Push Hook are posted
then: two hub.forge.push events are emitted
resource_id is the ref of each
tests.pseudocode: assert [e.EventType for e in events]==['hub.forge.push']*2

tests.title: Every relayed event has the fixed HubEvent fields and exactly the metadata keys of its kind
given: a bound workspace widgets and a recording emitter
tests.when: one delivery of each kind is posted: issue edited, issue labeled, comment created, pull request merged, push (GitHub) and a GitLab issue update
then: Workspace is widgets, ActorType is forge, ActorID is empty
ResourceType is issue, comment, pull_request or repository, ResourceID is the decimal number (iid for GitLab) or the ref for a push, Action is the last segment of the event type (push for a push)
metadata keys equal forge, target, delivery_id, actor plus: number,title,url,labels / number,label,labels,url / number,comment_url,pull_request / number,url,head,base,merged / ref,before,after

tests.title: Titles are cut to 256 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary and URLs never carry userinfo

tests.title: Each delivery and webhook event type is an exported constant in internal/audit/types.go equal to its string

given: a real DuckDB audit store, SSE manager and broadcast emitter

tests.title: An Emit error is logged and the remaining events are still emitted without changing the answer
given: an emitter that returns an error for the first event and records the rest
captured slog output
tests.when: a delivery producing three events is posted
